captured_cases.expected_outcome: After the generated migration, store a directed relationship from checkout tour B to prerequisite tour A. The generated reader identifies B as configured and returns A as its prerequisite. A and B are controlled examples derived from the owner flow, not production records.

Configure checkout tour B with prerequisite tours A and C. The reader preserves both prerequisites. It does not reduce the configured list to a single arbitrary prerequisite or require purchase at both. Purchase qualification itself remains outside this atom.
A tour absent from the configured checkout relationships is not reported as eligible and has no prerequisite tours returned. Availability of a discount code alone does not configure eligibility.
With only B-to-A configured, querying A must not infer eligibility or return B as a prerequisite. Relationships are directed, not symmetric.

Run the actual generated migration up and down only against an isolated database. It creates and removes the new relationship storage while preserving the pre-existing tours table and its recorded data. The relationship reader does not change tour data.
